question: What mechanisms drive re-entrant phase transitions in systems with paramagnetic ligands?
answer: Re-entrant phase transitions in systems with paramagnetic ligands are driven by the competition between magnetic interactions and lattice elasticity. In the La(hfac)₃(pyDTDA)₂ complex, these transitions arise from the sequential rupture of "pancake-bonded" π-radical dimers, which alters the magnetic moment and crystallographic symmetry. A microscopic model reveals that the softness of the lattice (low elastic constant, κ) allows magnetic interactions (singlet-triplet energy difference, A) to dominate, stabilizing a triclinic phase at intermediate temperatures before reverting to the original monoclinic phase. This mechanism is generalizable to other soft solids with isolated radical dimers, where tuning κ and A can control transition temperatures.

### Task 1: Summarize the Purpose of the Paper  
The paper investigates π-π radical interactions and their role in supramolecular recognition, focusing on their ability to induce switchable structural and magnetic properties. By studying the La(hfac)₃(pyDTDA)₂ coordination complex, the authors observe rare re-entrant phase transitions driven by "pancake bonding" between π-radical ligands. The paper develops a theoretical model that explains this behavior and extends the findings to predict re-entrant phase transitions in other systems with low lattice rigidity.
